Ruled out by code read: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh prune stage is ONE 'timeout 300 git prune' process (no loop); the in-process pollers fetch every 45 s (live_review_rows_watch POLL_S=45, directed_actions.POLL_S), not 1/s; wake poster read_auth_header runs 'git config --global --get-all' once per pass (config does not run gc --auto). The warning is printed by commands that run 'gc --auto' (fetch, commit, merge...), so the caller runs one of those about once a second under the git-sync unit's cgroup. LEADING HYPOTHESIS, UNPROVEN: the VM clone is a PARTIAL clone (deploy script fetches with --filter=blob:limit and sparse checkout); each missing blob read ('git show origin/main:<path>', 'git cat-file', reset/read-tree) triggers its own lazy promisor 'git fetch' child, one per blob, each printing the gc warning. Callers of per-call 'git show <ref>:' exist in src/runtime/checklist_store.py, live_review_rows.py, ltr_first_proof.py. TO NAME IT: a read-only 'ps -eo pid,ppid,etimes,cmd | grep git' snapshot during a sync, plus 'git config --get remote.origin.promisor'; needs an exec Approve (even read-only exec does), so fold it into the repack card's first step. 2026-11-16 19:31Z CALLER OF THE ~1/s GIT PROCESSES: strong evidence it is the sync's own 'git prune'. Journal windows 19:20-19:21 and 19:28-19:29Z: the 'too many unreachable loose objects' lines (new PID each, ~1/s) run continuously from the start of the prune stage and stop at the same second as '>>> WARNING: git prune failed or timed out' (19:20:55Z and 19:28:49Z); no such lines between prune end and the next stage except the hard-reset's. In a PARTIAL clone (the deploy fetch uses --filter=blob:limit) 'git prune' must walk reachability and lazily fetches each missing promisor object, one 'git fetch' child per object, each printing the gc warning. That is why prune never finishes in 300 s and why gc --prune / repack on this clone would behave the same. PLAN CHANGE for the repack step: do NOT run 'git prune' or 'git gc --prune' on this clone as planned (promisor fetch storm against GitHub on a saturated VM); the safe options to price first are (a) stop the deploy script running 'git prune' on a partial clone (it only wastes its 300 s timeout every sync: remove or gate the stage on 'git config remote.origin.promisor' != true), or (b) re-clone the VM tree full-depth into a fresh dir off-line.
